Hello Hal,

I’m following up again regarding the defective cooling fan on my BSB
NerdOctaxe 12TH/s miner, purchased August 18, 2026, for $424.48.

I appreciate your responses, but so far I’ve only been told that my request
has been forwarded to the team. I have yet to receive any actual
information regarding a warranty replacement or resolution.

This miner is barely two months old, and it’s disappointing to have a $400+
piece of equipment sitting idle because of a cooling fan that should not
have failed so soon.

I understand that warranty claims can take time, but I would appreciate a
definite answer regarding the following:

   1. Is the defective fan covered under warranty?
   2. Can a replacement fan be shipped to me at no charge?
   3. When can I reasonably expect a resolution?

I will be traveling out of state beginning November 2, so I would
appreciate an update before my departure, even if the replacement cannot be
shipped immediately.

I would much rather resolve this directly and amicably than have to pursue
other options.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to hearing from
someone who can provide a specific resolution.

Sincerely,

William L.
Handed to the team · Fan replacement part needs to be approved and shipped; I have no store or stock

Hello William,

Thank you for laying it out so clearly, and I am sorry you have been given nothing but "passed to the team" twice now. Here is the technical side, which is mine to answer, and I will be straight with you about the rest.

On the hardware: a failed cooling fan on a NerdOctaxe is not treated as a board fault here, which is good news for you. Our hardware lead's rule is that a fan, a screen, a stand, a plug or a power brick is handled by sending the part, not by sending the miner back. That means you would not be shipping a $400 miner across the country and waiting weeks for it. I have recorded my finding on your case as exactly that: the unit itself is sound, it needs a new cooling fan.

Two quick things worth trying while you wait, because they occasionally bring a fan back and cost you nothing. First, with the unit unplugged, unseat and reseat the fan connector on the board and check the blades are clear of dust, a cable or a sticker. Second, if your unit has a second fan header, move the fan plug to the other header and power up for a minute. If it spins on the other header, the header died and not the fan, which is still a part-level thing but useful for us to know. Please do not run the miner with a dead fan while you test, just long enough to see if the fan turns, since the NerdOctaxe will overheat quickly without airflow.

On your three questions, honestly: the part itself is a warranty-type part on a two-month-old unit, but I am not the person who can authorize a shipment or declare it free of charge, and I will not promise you something I cannot deliver. What I have done is put your case in front of the team with my finding and the part named, so they are not starting from zero. They are offline over the weekend and pick it up Monday at 10am ET, and the answer will come to you in this same email thread, so you will have it before you travel on November 2.

If you want a faster technical second opinion in the meantime, our Discord is very active at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and you can mention @nullhashrate, who is our hardware lead.

Sincerely,
Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Hello Bill,

Thank you for trying, and I appreciate you doing it from six hours away. Unfortunately the video did not come through on my end, the message arrived with no attachment. That happens often with larger video files on email, so if you still have it, a good workaround is to upload it to Google Drive, Dropbox or YouTube as unlisted and paste the link in a reply. Any length is fine, ten seconds of the fan with the sound is plenty.

If the file is simply gone, do not worry about chasing it. A short written description does most of the job: whether it is the front or the back fan, and whether it has stopped completely or is spinning slowly, rattling, grinding or cutting in and out. That alone tells us whether the fan bearing has gone or the header on the board is at fault, and both of those are part-level, not a board fault.

Leaving it unplugged until you are home on November 20 is exactly the right call, so nothing is being made worse in the meantime. The checks I mentioned, reseating the fan connector and trying the other fan header, can wait until you are back in front of it.

On the replacement side, your case is with the team with my finding already attached, they are back today at 10am Eastern and the answer comes to you in this thread. If you want a quick second opinion on the fan noise in the meantime, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and you can mention @nullhashrate, our hardware lead.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Looking at the front of the miner, the large,  right-hand fan has stopped

Hello Bill,

That is exactly the detail I needed, thank you. A fan that stops and then catches again on its own for a while is the classic signature of a seized or dying bearing in the fan itself. It is not a sign of anything wrong with the hashboard or the controller, and it is not caused by anything you did. Fans are the one moving part in these units and they are the first thing to wear out, sometimes early.

I have recorded my technical finding on your case as a fan fault on the large right-hand fan viewed from the front, with the miner itself sound, so nobody is going to ask you to ship a $400 unit anywhere over this.

When you are back home on November 20, two things are worth doing before the fan goes on. First, with the unit unplugged, unplug and firmly reseat that fan's connector on the board, since a half-seated plug gives the exact same stop-start behavior. Second, if your board has a spare fan header, move that fan's plug to it and power up briefly. If the fan then runs steadily, the fault is the header and not the fan, which is still useful to know. If it stutters on both headers, the fan is finished, as I expect.

In the meantime, please keep the miner unplugged as you have been doing. A NerdOctaxe running with one of its main fans stalled will climb into thermal throttling quickly and there is no reason to risk the chips for a few hours of hashing.

Your request for the replacement fan is in front of the team now with my finding attached, and they are working today, so the answer on that side will come to you in this thread.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Thank you!

--
Sincerely,
Bill L.
(phone hidden)

Hello Bill,

You are very welcome. Nothing more is needed from you right now, so enjoy the rest of your trip.

When you are home on November 20 and have tried the connector reseat and the spare header, just reply here with what the fan did and I will pick it straight back up. If anything else about the miner looks odd when you power it up again, temperatures, hashrate or the screen, send me what you see and we will sort that out too.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
